title: RynnWorld-Teleop: Digital Teleoperation for Robot Data
hook: Collecting robot demonstrations means binding an operator's time to one physical robot. RynnWorld-Teleop swaps in a world model: move your hands, and it generates the footage instead.
key_points: Introduces 'digital teleoperation': a generative world model stands in for the physical robot, decoupling data collection from hardware.
An operator's hand-pose stream drives the model to synthesize realistic egocentric robot video from a single reference image.
The recorded pose stream is an embodiment-agnostic action label, retargetable to any target robot via standard retargeting.
Streaming autoregressive distillation compresses generation to single-pass inference: 40+ FPS in real time on one H100 GPU.
Policies trained purely on this generated data reach zero-shot sim-to-real transfer; mixing in real data lifts success rates further.
content_html: Scaling robot learning needs more demonstrations than physical teleoperation can supply — every session ties an operator's time to one specific robot and room. RynnWorld-Teleop proposes cutting that cord entirely: replace the physical robot with a generative world model.
extra_html: The system streams an operator's hand-pose input into a video Diffusion Transformer that synthesizes high-fidelity egocentric robot footage from a single reference image, using depth-aware skeletal conditioning and progressive human-to-robot training. Because the recorded action label is the hand-pose stream itself rather than a robot-specific trajectory, it's embodiment-agnostic — standard retargeting can map it onto any target robot, turning one recording into state-action data for many robots at once. Streaming autoregressive distillation then compresses the generative process into single-pass inference, reaching 40+ FPS real-time generation on a single H100 GPU. Policies trained exclusively on this generated data achieve zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across dexterous, diverse bimanual tasks, and mixing the generated data into real-world datasets consistently pushes success rates higher. Haoyu Zhao and colleagues, arXiv 2026 (67 HF community upvotes).

related.title: RynnWorld-4D: RGB-Depth-Flow World Models for Robot Manipulation
related.hook: A robot needs to know how a scene's 3D structure will move, not just what it looks like. This world model predicts RGB, depth, and optical flow together, then hands the result straight to a policy.

related.title: GigaWorld-1: World Models as Robot Policy Evaluators
related.hook: Testing a robot policy for real means slow, costly rollouts. GigaWorld-1 asks whether a video world model can judge a policy instead — and finds visual realism is the wrong thing to optimize for.

related.title: World Action Models: A Survey
related.hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.

flashcards.prompt: What problem does 'digital teleoperation' solve, and how?
flashcards.back_html: Physical teleoperation binds every demonstration to one robot and workspace. Digital teleoperation replaces the real robot with a generative world model, driven purely by the operator's hand movements.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the recorded hand-pose stream called an 'embodiment-agnostic' action label?

choices.text: It isn't tied to one robot's joints — it can be retargeted to any target robot via standard retargeting
It only works with the exact robot used during recording
It requires re-recording separately for each robot embodiment
It is a text description rather than a pose signal

flashcards.explanation_html: Because the label is a hand-pose stream, not a robot-specific joint trajectory, standard retargeting can map it onto any target robot's action space — one recording, many embodiments.

flashcards.prompt: What real-world result did policies trained purely on RynnWorld-Teleop-generated data achieve?
flashcards.back_html: Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across dexterous, diverse bimanual tasks — with no real robot data in training. Adding this generated data to real datasets further improved success rates.
